Hours of direct sun over a day

Source: R/shade.R
sun_hours.Rd

Sun positions every step minutes over the local day (at the middle of each step), one shadow sweep each, summed.

Usage

sun_hours(
  z,
  extent = NULL,
  date,
  lon,
  lat,
  tz = "UTC",
  step = 10,
  far = NULL,
  far_extent = NULL,
  convergence = 0
)

Arguments

z

matrix of heights, row 1 at the north edge, square cells; or the result of gdalraster::read_ds() (a vector with a gis attribute), in which case extent is taken from it

extent

c(xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) of z

date

the day, a Date or "YYYY-MM-DD", local to tz

lon, lat

where the sun is computed from (the middle of the grid, say), degrees

tz

time zone of date

step

minutes between sun positions

far, far_extent

optional coarser grid surrounding z (and its extent), for terrain further out; its cells that touch z are skipped

convergence

grid azimuth of true north (meridian convergence, degrees), added to azimuth; 0 for a grid aligned with true north. In polar stereographic (EPSG:3031, EPSG:3413 style) it is the longitude, or minus it in the north

Value

matrix like z of hours of direct sun, with attributes daylight (hours the sun is above a flat horizon) and extent

Examples

## Maungawhau, Auckland
z <- volcano[nrow(volcano):1, ncol(volcano):1]
ex <- c(2667400, 2668010, 6478700, 6479570)
h <- sun_hours(z, ex, "2026-06-21", lon = 174.764, lat = -36.876,
               tz = "Pacific/Auckland", step = 20)
range(h)
#> [1] 0.000000 9.666667
